t-desktop.text: Desktop — a code chat splits its column: the checkout on the left, the chat on the right

t-phone.text: Phone — one screen, a Chat / Code switch in the title bar

n-layout.text:
Layout

The split lives inside the chat's main column, not the viewport, so it comes and goes with the app menu. Default 70 / 30, a drag handle between, remembered per browser; chat never narrower than 320 px. The chat pane uses its existing compact title bar (overflow menu) whenever it is under 640 px — measured on the pane, not the window.

Under about 1024 px of column the same two panes become the two tabs.

n-save.text:
Save ≠ commit

Save writes the file into the checkout on the sandbox worker — the same place the chat's tools write — uncommitted. Commit records whatever is in the working tree (yours and the chat's) as the person, on the current branch or a new one. Push stays a separate step, with the person's own Bitbucket grant, exactly as the tools do it.

n-conflict.text:
Who else is writing

The checkout is shared with the chat's turn and with other members. Every read carries a content hash; a save sends it back and is refused when the file moved underneath — the amber banner in board 2. While a turn runs, a file the turn wrote is reloaded on turn end unless it has unsaved edits, in which case the banner offers Compare / Reload theirs / Keep mine.

n-model.text:
The chat knows what you did

A save and a commit from the editor each add a small note row to the transcript (like the auto-mode nudge rows): the thread shows it, the Changes panel counts the commit, and the next turn's model sees that a person edited those files by hand instead of finding a surprise in git status.

n-scope.text:
Not in the first cut

• Follow the assistant (editor jumps to the file a turn is writing)
• Diff markers against HEAD inside the editor gutter
• Multi-cursor / find-and-replace across files
• Creating, renaming or deleting files from the pane (the chat's tools do it)
• Before a chat has cloned: the tree and files come from Bitbucket read-only, as the project page's tree already does
